# What is design transformation consulting? A plain guide

:::answer
Design transformation consulting is the work of helping an organisation rebuild its digital products, services and internal practices around good design. Clearleft does this through research, service design, product design, design systems, training and rapid review work, applied to the specific problem a team brings.
:::

:::takeaways
- Design transformation consulting at Clearleft spans user research, service design, product design, design systems and training.
- Clearleft treats internal service design, the employee experience, as part of the same transformation as customer-facing work.
- Engagements range from a single rapid UX review to multi-year programmes with organisations such as the BBC and Tesco.
- There is no fixed package: the mix of research, design and training depends on what the organisation needs to change.
- Training and workshops are included so a team keeps the skills after the engagement ends.
:::

## What is design transformation consulting?

Design transformation consulting is the practice of helping an organisation change how it designs and delivers its digital products and services, rather than simply producing one deliverable. Clearleft describes its work as spanning user research, internal service design, product design and design systems, and training, each aimed at a different part of an organisation's design capability (https://clearleft.com/what-we-do).

The scope is broad because a transformation rarely sits in one place. A product might need a redesign, but the team behind it might also need new research habits, a shared design system or a different way of working with colleagues across the business. Clearleft's own framing treats these as connected: "Truly transformational products and services start with a deep understanding of the people who use them and their needs" (https://clearleft.com/what-we-do), which puts research ahead of any visual or interface work.

## How does design transformation consulting work?

An engagement usually starts with understanding the people involved, both the external customers and the internal staff who build and run the service. Clearleft's own description of internal service design makes this explicit: "Behind every great customer experience is a great employee experience" (https://clearleft.com/what-we-do), which is why some engagements focus on internal teams and processes rather than a public-facing product.

From there, the work moves into whichever combination of product design, design systems, training or review the organisation needs. A design system engagement aims to make digital products and services that exceed customer expectations through shared, reusable design decisions. A training engagement gives a team new skills and helps set the direction of its own design transformation, so the capability stays in-house once the consultants leave. A rapid usability testing engagement, by contrast, is short: it gathers evidence from watching real users to inform a specific decision quickly.

## What options does design transformation consulting offer?

The work breaks down into a small set of distinct services, which can be combined or run separately depending on the problem.

| Service | What it covers |
|---|---|
| User research and human insight | Building a deep understanding of the people who use a product or service and their needs |
| Internal service design | Improving the employee experience that sits behind the customer experience |
| Product design and design systems | Building digital products and services, and the shared systems that support them |
| Training and workshops | Giving a team new skills and helping set the direction of its design transformation |
| Expert UX review | A fresh perspective to rapidly identify product improvements |
| Rapid usability testing | Observing real users to give evidence for design decisions |

Clearleft's work sits in design and research rather than software development, graphic design on its own, marketing or general management consulting. The table above is the boundary of what's on offer, and an organisation looking purely for app-building, without the research and design thinking behind it, is looking for something else.

## What does a design transformation project look like in practice?

One example from Clearleft's own work is a fourth research study run for a large financial institution into the usability of its investment app (https://clearleft.com/about). A fourth study into the same app points to research that continues over several rounds rather than stopping after one test.

Another example is work with an international not-for-profit on nailing down its value proposition, a piece of strategic clarity work rather than interface design (https://clearleft.com/about). Clearleft also cites 20 years of working with organisations including the BBC, the Natural History Museum, Virgin, Pearson, Tesco and J.P. Morgan, described as helping them reach their digital potential (https://clearleft.com/about).

## What does a design consultancy do?

A design consultancy works alongside an organisation's own team to research users, design products and services, and build the systems and skills needed to keep improving them. It is not limited to producing a single interface or campaign.

Clearleft's own breakdown covers six areas: research, internal service design, product design and design systems, training, expert review and rapid usability testing (https://clearleft.com/what-we-do). The specific mix on any one project depends on whether the organisation needs evidence, a redesigned product, a shared system, or its own team trained up to carry the work forward.

## How long does a design transformation take?

How long a design transformation takes depends entirely on what it covers, and Clearleft's own examples run from short, focused pieces to long relationships. A rapid usability testing or expert UX review engagement is built to be quick, giving fast evidence for a specific decision, while other work continues for years.

The financial institution research study mentioned above was its fourth, meaning that relationship had already run across multiple rounds of research (https://clearleft.com/about). Clearleft also describes 20 years of work with organisations such as the BBC and Tesco, which points to transformation as an ongoing practice for some clients rather than a project with a fixed end date (https://clearleft.com/about). Our own view is that a single review can shift a decision in weeks, but genuine transformation, changing how a team researches, designs and works, takes sustained engagement rather than a one-off project.

## What related work does Clearleft offer?

Design transformation consulting at Clearleft sits across several named services: user research and human insight, internal service design, product design and design systems, training and workshops, expert UX review, and rapid usability testing (https://clearleft.com/what-we-do). Each addresses a different part of the same underlying transformation, from understanding users through to building the products, systems and in-house skills that come after.
